claims.text: Stable, coherent protective-scale formation in CrFeCoNiX alloys is primarily governed by synergy between Cr and Al in a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
During exposure above 900 °C, Cr diffuses outward and contributes to outward-growing oxide scales.
Cr and Al undergo synchronized or controlled outward diffusion in homogeneous CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Coupled Cr and Al diffusion nucleates a continuous, slow-growing (Cr,Al)2O3-type scale.
Al2O3 is protective, grows more slowly than chromium oxide, and is comparatively stable in aggressive high-temperature environments.
A continuous (Cr,Al)2O3-type scale minimizes internal stress and resists cracking and spallation.
Chemical and microstructural heterogeneity in multiphase alloys produces spatially variable and complex oxide structures.
Elemental segregation causes localized differences in oxidation kinetics.
CrMnFeCoNi can form temperature-dependent manganese oxides, including a transition from Mn2O3 to Mn3O4 between 800 and 900 °C.
Failure to form a Cr2O3 layer can permit further outward Mn diffusion and Mn3O4 formation near 950 °C.
Localized Mn- or Si-containing oxides necessarily create uneven scale growth, internal stress, cracking, and spallation.
Single-phase, Cr- and Al-rich CrFeCoNiX samples, especially CrFeCoNiAl, will form thin, coherent, adherent scales that persist above 900 °C.
Multiphase, segregated samples will exhibit more heterogeneous oxide layers, cracking, spallation, and poorer oxidation or corrosion resistance.
Alloys with X = Si or Mn will perform worse than otherwise comparable alloys with X = Al.
NiCr-based alloys are suitable protective-chromia reference materials under comparable high-temperature conditions.
Above 900 °C, chromia may form volatile CrO3, potentially limiting the persistence of a chromia-containing scale.
Oxide structures in multicomponent HEAs depend on complex chemistry, surface heterogeneity, microstructure, and high-temperature phase instability.
Published conclusions about CrMnFeCoNi oxidation remain ambiguous and vary with post-oxidation analysis assumptions.

contradictions.description: The material family includes nominal CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn compositions, which contain no Al as stated, but the proposed general mechanism requires local Al and synchronized Cr-Al diffusion. The mechanism is therefore not compositionally applicable to all listed X variants without an additional Al addition.

The hypothesis predicts persistence of a Cr-containing protective scale above 900 °C, while the cited basis also states that chromia can become volatile as CrO3 above 900 °C. The hypothesis does not specify when Al stabilizes the scale sufficiently to overcome this limitation.
